elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Clause (b) as rendered reads "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED...", replacing the Licensor-only cap.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The cap is "THE FEES PAID BY LICENSEE ... IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — no USD 1,000,000 floor and "paid" only, not "paid or payable".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Clause (a) is untouched and still runs one way: "IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE TO LICENSEE ... FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES". To meet this, (a) would need to be recast as "NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "EACH PARTY'S LIABILITY SHALL BE UNCAPPED FOR ... ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list contains only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out was added.
"THE LIMITATION IN SECTION (b) ABOVE SHALL NOT APPLY TO ... ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS".
Carve-out sentence expressly lists "ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE".
Fraud does not appear anywhere in the amended Article XIII carve-out list.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out was added; indeed retained clause (a) still exculpates Licensor entirely for third-party IP infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language states that Licensee's obligation to pay fees is outside the cap; the new mutual cap in (b) applies to "EITHER PARTY'S" total liability without a payment-obligation carve-out.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Amended (b): "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED..." — the one-sided Licensor-only cap is removed and Licensee is now capped as well.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "...EXCEED THE FEES PAID BY LICENSEE TO LICENSOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — the prior "ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID" basis is gone; "Fees ... under this Agreement" is not narrowed to a token defined subset.
New sentence disapplies the (b) limitation and makes each party's liability uncapped for "ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same sentence covers "ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS", mutually.
"...ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" is expressly outside the cap.
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" is named in the uncapped carve-out sentence; spelling variant is immaterial.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original (b) capped only Licensor at one half of amounts paid (well below 6 months' fees) and left Licensee uncapped — walk-away territory on two counts.

Fallback is complete: the cap is mutual, based on fees paid by Licensee in the 12 months preceding the claim, and indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are expressly carved out for each party.

Preferred is not reached — no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" rather than "paid or payable", clause (a)'s consequential-damages exclusion remains Licensor-only, and there are no data protection/security, fraud, IP-infringement or Customer-payment-obligation carve-outs. Those are noted as trade-room, not defects in the chosen level.

Minimality holds: only clause (b) was rewritten and one carve-out sentence added; clause (a) and clause (c) are retained verbatim, no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages categories were bolted on.

Intent is preserved: the added sentence cross-refers accurately to "SECTION (b) ABOVE", introduces no undefined term, and no retained sentence contradicts the new mutual cap. Drafting nit only — the rationale calls the new sentence "(d)" but it is rendered unlabelled after (c); adding the "(d)" designation would tidy the article without changing substance.
